target: 谷 in 僕谷 of the Jié couplet
reason: The graph 谷 was historically polyphonic, and non-default readings are themselves attested in Inner-Asian names/titles. Therefore lexical-frequency priors from ordinary Chinese cannot be used as a decisive transcription prior in a foreign-language couplet.

sources.citation: Vovin, Vajda & de la Vaissière 2016, Journal Asiatique 304(1):125-144, DOI 10.2143/JA.304.1.3146838
evidence: Their Chart 1 lists multiple historical readings for 谷 across reconstruction systems rather than a single value.
They criticize Shimunek et al.'s selection of *lok as a northern-frontier reading because no source is supplied for that contextual claim.
They argue the k-initial reading is overall the most frequent/common reading, while explicitly acknowledging the l- and y-initial reading families.

sources.citation: Baxter & Sagart 2014 reconstruction list / Old Chinese: A New Reconstruction
evidence: The ordinary 'valley' lexeme 谷 has Middle Chinese kuwk and Old Chinese *C.qˤok in Baxter-Sagart.
This independently anchors a k-initial reading family but does not establish that a foreign transcription in the fourth century must select that reading.

sources.citation: Traditional Middle Chinese reading traditions as indexed in modern historical dictionaries
evidence: 谷 also has Middle Chinese luwk, preserved specifically in 谷蠡, a Xiongnu official title.
谷 also has Middle Chinese yowk, preserved specifically in 吐谷渾 / 谷渾, an Inner-Asian ethnonym/name context.
Because rare readings occur precisely in foreign-name/title contexts, 'default Chinese lexical frequency' is not a safe prior for the couplet's phonographic use.

model_rule.old: Treat luk vs kok as a binary major divergence to be solved before language comparison.
model_rule.new: Treat 谷 reading as a latent categorical variable {K,L,Y}. Run candidate models across all admissible reading states. Do not reward a model simply for choosing the reading state it needs.
model_rule.penalty: Apply a reading-selection patch cost only if a model requires one state while independently dated transcription evidence favors another. Until then, marginalize/neutralize this position rather than hard-pick it.

information_gain_update.why: The audit establishes that the uncertainty is real and context-sensitive, but not presently identifiable from the graph alone. More effort on 谷 is lower-yield than auditing the morphology that flips the ablation leader.
information_gain_update.new_top_question: Can the proposed Arin -taŋ/-aŋ and internal verb-template slots be verified independently of the Jié couplet, without circular reuse of the same analysis?

FACT: 谷 has multiple historical reading traditions.
k-, l-, and y/j-initial reading families are represented in Middle Chinese reconstruction traditions.
The l- and y/j-initial readings occur in Inner-Asian name/title contexts such as 谷蠡 and 吐谷渾.
INFERENCE: Foreign transcription context weakens the prior that the ordinary k-initial lexical reading must have been intended in the couplet.
谷 alone should therefore have low discriminatory weight between Old Arin and Turkic until an independent local transcription convention is found.
OPEN: Which exact reading was intended in the Jié couplet.
Whether the l-initial reading used in 谷蠡 reflects the same regional/transcriptional convention relevant to the couplet.
